title: Quantum Groups at Roots of Unity and Tilting Quotients

items.title: De Concini–Kac, Lusztig, and small quantum-group forms at a root of unity
items.statement: Fix the generic Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra, its Cartan lattice and an admissible root parameter. Define the De Concini–Kac specialization, the Lusztig divided-power specialization and the root-power quotient convention used for the small quantum group. The definition makes no injectivity, Frobenius, finite-dimensionality, semisimplicity, or category-equivalence assertion.
items.strategy: Specify the base rings, specialization maps, root-order conditions, Cartan lattice and the three constructions; separate generic inclusion from the map after specialization.
items.axiom_use: None; these are explicit algebraic definitions.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych, and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories
sources.locator: Chapter 5, §§5.6–5.7, printed pp. 101–104: the rank-one De Concini–Kac and Lusztig forms, the small quantum group, and the limits of the general Cartan construction.

sources.locator: §3.5.1–3.5.2, PDF pp. 17–18: the rank-one forms, root-power quotient and Hopf-map directions; the source explicitly leaves the higher-rank defining relations to the literature.

items.title: Tilting modules and negligible morphisms in a root-of-unity category
items.statement: Given a supplied C-linear additive rigid braided monoidal category of finite-dimensional type-1 modules with pivotal structure and trace, plus specified finite-dimensional standard and dual-standard module families, define filtrations, tilting objects, negligible morphism subspaces, and candidate quotient morphism spaces. This definition asserts no closure of negligible morphisms under tensor product, no quotient semisimplicity, no modularity, and no fusion-rule theorem.
items.strategy: State the category, module-family, filtration, trace, and quotient data as explicit inputs, and define each term without assuming the desired closure or semisimplicity properties.
items.axiom_use: None; the definition uses only the supplied category and trace data.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych, and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories
sources.locator: §8.18.2, printed pp. 235–236: the simply-laced, large-root-order tilting quotient and alcove labels; the construction is referred to Andersen–Paradowski rather than proved there.

items.title: The rank-one root-power quotient is a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra
items.statement: For a primitive odd root of unity $\zeta$ of order $\ell>2$, the rank-one De Concini–Kac specialization has PBW basis $\{F^aK^bE^c:a,c\ge0,\ b\in\mathbb Z\}$. The ideal generated by $E^\ell,F^\ell,K^\ell-1$ is stable under the local Hopf maps, and the quotient has basis $\{F^aK^bE^c:0\le a,b,c<\ell\}$ and dimension $\ell^3$.
items.strategy: Prove spanning by terminating normal-order rewriting, use the generic rank-one PBW supplier for independence over the integral base ring, compute root-power commutators and coproducts, and then read off the quotient basis.
items.axiom_use: None; the rewriting, geometric sums and finite q-binomial calculation are explicit and choice-free.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof and Mykola Semenyakin, A Brief Introduction to Quantum Groups

items.title: The rank-one De Concini–Kac to Lusztig specialization map is not injective
items.statement: At every primitive odd root $\zeta$ of order $\ell>2$, the generator map from the rank-one De Concini–Kac specialization to the Lusztig divided-power specialization kills the nonzero source element $E^\ell$; hence the map is not injective.
items.strategy: Establish the generator map from the root-specialized commutator relation, evaluate the divided-power identity at the root, and use the proved De Concini–Kac PBW basis to separate zero in source from zero in target.
items.axiom_use: None; the map and the nonzero PBW monomial are explicit.

title: Quantum Groups at Roots of Unity and Tilting Quotients: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The rank-one small quantum group at a primitive fifth root has dimension 125
items.statement: For a primitive fifth root $\zeta$, the rank-one root-power quotient has the 125-element PBW basis given by the exponents $0,1,2,3,4$ on $F,K,E$.
items.strategy: Specialize the proved rank-one PBW quotient at $\ell=5$ and enumerate its bounded exponent basis.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a finite explicit specialization.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof and Mykola Semenyakin, A Brief Introduction to Quantum Groups
sources.locator: §3.5.1, PDF p. 18: the rank-one small-quantum-group quotient; the example substitutes $\ell=5$ into the locally proved basis.

items.title: Specialization does not preserve injectivity of the rank-one form inclusion
items.statement: The assertion that the natural map from the De Concini–Kac specialization to the Lusztig divided-power specialization is injective for every odd root order is false.
items.strategy: Use the explicit fifth-root specialization to exhibit a nonzero source element mapped to zero.
items.axiom_use: None; the witness is the single PBW monomial $E^5$.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof and Mykola Semenyakin, A Brief Introduction to Quantum Groups
sources.locator: §3.5.2, PDF pp. 18–19: the specialized inclusion is explicitly not an inclusion; the example computes the $\ell=5$ witness locally.
